shortcut_name: Johnson's rule for two-machine flow shop
evidence: The survivor says: "early.append((p1, p2))", "late.append((p1, p2))", and "sort early by increasing p1, late by decreasing p2".
affordance_in_statement: The Main Stage hosts the live acts consecutively in the exact order of your lineup... The Review Room also hosts the critique sessions in that exact same lineup order... its critique session... begins at the earliest possible moment.
secondary_shortcut_name: Use the same permutation on both venues
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this structure: it is the core of the task. To obscure it without changing the task, present the schedule through event-release and precedence constraints rather than explicitly describing two venues processing jobs in the same order.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes the problem as a two-machine flow-shop makespan minimization and applies Johnson's ordering.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The Review Room also hosts the critique sessions in that exact same lineup order, with each critique starting when both the corresponding live act and the previous critique have completed.

common_affordance: The explicit two-machine flow-shop structure: both stages process every performance in one common order, and the second-stage start time is the maximum of its release time and the previous second-stage completion.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It sorts solely by review duration descending, ignoring the Johnson partition and the interaction between Main Stage completion times and Review Room durations.
It orders jobs by descending min(p1, p2), which is not the pairwise-exchange ordering required for two-machine flow-shop minimization.
It sorts by p2 descending and consequently misses the dependence of the optimal order on both processing times.

recommended_edit: Replace the rule that the Review Room must use the exact same lineup order with a rule allowing critiques to be selected independently from currently completed live acts. This removes the common Johnson-rule structure while preserving the numeric bounds, input format, output format, and example values.
regression_risk: Changing the second-stage ordering rule changes the underlying scheduling problem; a previously defeated heuristic could become correct for some instances of the new problem.
